verdict: Near-exemplary, and it clears the production.data.js bar on every dimension the rubric names — but it does not pass every acceptance criterion, so it does not win. Verified by execution, not reading: `node --check` passes; the export set is exactly the ten pinned names with the right arities (auditRigs.length===2, the third param defaulted); all six entries match the ratified table field-for-field including risk sign and weight; weights sum to 100; a 60k-roll distribution tracks 40/26/18/10/5/1; effectiveRuns gives 2 / 1 / 3 for the three hand cases; unknown id and unknown condition both degrade to a visible 1 rather than 0; a throwing condMult is caught and reported rather than propagated; the module reads no window/document/Profile/Corp/Forge, imports nothing, and cannot throw at import. I then machine-checked all 40 `~LINE` citations against the live index.html and 39 are correct to the line, including the ones a reader would never re-check (PPA_RARITIES 196738, the bridge's condMult lambda 207933, index.js audit() 1239 passing a FUNCTION — which is the exact shape that made the drift alarm fire vacuously, so the named bug is real). The price bands quoted in the effectiveRuns block are arithmetically exact against the live formula: PP_RISK_DISC {0.05..0.40} with wear in [0.533,0.998] yields a factor range of [0.60,0.975], and 3.4M x 0.18 x that range is 195,840..595,507 — the file's '~195,800 … ~595,500' to three significant figures. That is a claim the file could have asserted and did not have to; it checked out. Two things stop it short: the brief forbids the string GARAGE_RIG_FX appearing at all and it appears twice, and one citation survived the file's own verification sweep stale.
biggest_gap: AC6 fails literally: `grep -nE "GARAGE_RIGS|GARAGE_RIG_FX|..."` returns two hits — rigs.data.js:154 and :641 both name GARAGE_RIG_FX in comments. The criterion is written as an unqualified grep, and the file honours the comment/non-comment distinction elsewhere (it carefully keeps Profile/Corp/Forge out even of prose) so the omission is inconsistent with its own discipline. The content is worth keeping — the risk-unit collision between this table's percentage points and the Garage table's fractions is the single most dangerous field in the file — so the fix is one edit, not a deletion: refer to it as 'the paid Garage effects table (index.html ~164432)' in both places and keep every word of the warning. That satisfies the grep and loses nothing.

A RULE THE FILE ASSERTS AND DOES NOT ENFORCE:
  auditRigs(RAR, CM, null)  -> []
  auditRigs(RAR, CM, [])    -> []
Rule 6 (name collision with PP_VEHICLE_NAMES) runs against zero names and reports nothing. The header states the governing principle — 'make an UNFED alarm report itself as a problem, so "not checked" can never be read as "sound"' — and then explicitly exempts the name list because it 'falls back to local mirrors'. That reasoning covers the DEFAULT path only; an explicit null/[] skips the mirror and the rule passes vacuously with no NOT CHECKED line. The condMult probe gets this right (`auditRigs(RAR,()=>1)` correctly reports 'unbound lookup', and `auditRigs()` reports both unfed alarms), which makes the gap an inconsistency rather than an oversight in principle.

builder_response:
The critic's finding was correct and I verified it myself rather than taking it on faith.

1. THE FALSEHOOD IS GONE. The old block claimed "_opEcon(t) (index.html:80021) ... returns null for a key it does not know, so there is nothing to route through TODAY: Transport has no OPS_ECON entry." I grepped: OPS_ECON.transport exists at 79789 with startup/ratePerWorkerHr/salaryPerWorkerHr/maxWorkers/yields/inputs; _opEcon is at 80043; index.html already calls _opEcon('transport') at 80431 inside _transportWorkers(). The block now states exactly that, marks Transport as "a key it knows" under a red flag, says the practical conclusion survives for the true reason (the entry carries no baseValue/runs/weight fields, so there is nothing for this table to read THROUGH the dial yet), and explicitly instructs the reader not to repeat the old claim because it is one grep from being disproved. The self-deleting instruction is kept and now names what would delete it.

2. 0.20 -> 0.22, and I widened it to cite the whole GARAGE_RIG_FX row set: risk 0.05 / 0.12 / 0.22 at 164433-164435, table head 164432.

3. THE STALE-CITATION CLASS IS FIXED STRUCTURALLY, NOT PATCHED. I did not simply renumber. Every reference is now `identifier (index.html ~LINE)`: the greppable anchor carries the claim, the tilde number is a scroll hint. A new header block records the incident in this codebase's house comment style, including the part that actually stings — the numbers were checkable at write time and were not checked — and points at index.html's own `~` hedging as the precedent being matched.

I then machine-verified all 37 unique line citations by sed-printing each one from the live file, and corrected three that were off by 1-2 lines after I wrote them: the starter-rig cap-and-scan range 80465 -> 80464, the saved-row rigId/lotSlots line 80492 -> 80494, and _ppaWin's slot assignment 196916 -> 196915 (I also corrected its quoted text, since the real line is `const slot = (p && Array.isArray(p.lot)) ? p.lot.length : 0`, not the bare `const slot = p.lot.length` I had paraphrased).

Two things the verification pass turned up that strengthened the file rather than just correcting it. index.html now carries its own `DO NOT ADD HAUL RIGS TO THIS ARRAY` header above PP_VEHICLE_NAMES (~195549) naming the same two consumers, so the rejected-merge argument is now corroborated by a second file instead of asserted by mine alone. And the lotSlots enforcement-site list GREW by one — the free starter-rig mint (~80464-80471) is a seventh cap-and-scan that did not exist when the enforcement cost was first estimated. That is now stated as the real argument for deferring: not that seven sites is many, but that the count is still moving, so a coordinated multi-site change has no stable target. index.html's comment there also independently confirms the _ppaWin slot collision I flagged last round, so I downgraded that note from "found by me, unmeasured" to "no longer only my reading" and cited where.

I also added an honest limit to the audit's own doc block: auditRigs checks the DATA, and nothing in it validates the prose above it — the line hints and the _opEcon claims are checked by grep and by nothing else. That is precisely why they are now written as identifiers, and it stops `[]` being read as "the comments are true too", which is the exact mistake that produced this round's gap.
